title: JWST's PEARLS: A Clumpy Ring Galaxy at z = 4.0148
question: Whether a ring-like galaxy candidate at z_spec = 4.0148 on the periphery of MACS0416 is a high-redshift collisional ring galaxy or a galaxy-galaxy strong gravitational lens.

what.value: Spectroscopic redshift z_spec = 4.0148 and NIRSpec PRISM spectrum from CANUCS Data Release 1

evidence.quote: cataloged as CANUCS 3100560 in the CAnadian NIRISS Unbiased Cluster Survey (Sarrouh et al. 2026) with a spectroscopic redshift _z_ spec = 4 _._ 0148.
We also make use of a publicly available NIRSpec PRISM spectrum of the source from the CANUCS Data Release 1, as detailed in Sarrouh et al. (2026).

what.value: Reduced ALMA Band 6 continuum mosaic of MACS0416 from ALCS

evidence.quote: MACS0416 was also observed as part of an ALMA Large Program (2018.1.00035.L; PI: K. Kohno), the ALMA Lensing Cluster Survey (ALCS; Fujimoto et al. 2024), using the Band 6 receiver.
Reduced data products for the cluster have been made available on the ALCS website

what.value: Catalog of local ring galaxies from the GALAXY CRUISE survey

evidence.loc: 5.1. Comparison to high-redshift ring galaxy candidates
evidence.quote: For the local galaxy sample, we utilize a catalog of ring galaxies from the GALAXY CRUISE survey (Shimakawa et al. 2024)

what.value: SFR and stellar masses of local galaxies from the GALEX-SDSS-WISE Legacy Catalog (GSWLC)

evidence.loc: 5.1. Comparison to high-redshift ring galaxy candidates
evidence.quote: We then crossmatch these galaxies to the GALEX-SDSS-WISE Legacy Catalog (GSWLC; Salim et al. 2016, 2018) for SFR and stellar masses derived from `CIGALE` (Boquien et al. 2019)

what.value: Comparison samples of strong gravitational lenses (SLACS, BELLS, SL2S, AGEL, PEARLS NEP, COWLS)

evidence.quote: Source versus lens redshift for a sample of well-characterized, optically selected strong lensing systems (SLACS, BELLS, SL2S; Bolton et al. 2008; Brownstein et al. 2012; Sonnenfeld et al. 2013, respectively) as compiled in Tan et al. (2024)
along with a recent release of strong lenses from the AGEL survey (Barone et al. 2026) and JWST-selected lenses in the PEARLS NEP time domain field (Ferrami et al. 2026).
and over 400 candidate gravitationally lensed systems in the COWLS program (Nightingale et al. 2025).

external_data.citation: Tan et al. (2024); Barone et al. (2026); Ferrami et al. (2026); Nightingale et al. (2025)

recipe.goal: Measure ring radius and ALMA dust continuum flux and mass
recipe.method: Fit an ellipse around the ring in CARTA to estimate the radius; measure the 261.3 GHz continuum flux density from the ALCS map, scale it to 870 um, and convert to dust mass using a scaling relation.
assumptions: Redshift-independent dust mass scaling relation from Dudzeviciute et al. (2020)

recipe.goal: PSF matching and multi-band aperture photometry
recipe.method: Generate and resample HST ACS and JWST NIRCam PSFs to 0.02'', create matching kernels to convolve all bands to the F444W resolution (FWHM ~ 0.16''), and extract photometry in apertures for the center, three clumps, and total system.
key_parameters: Aperture radius = 0.08'' for clumps A, B, C and center; 0.48'' for total system
assumptions: 5% systematic error added in quadrature to photometric measurements

recipe.goal: SED modeling of the CRG, clumps, and nearby companions
recipe.method: Fit multi-band HST and JWST photometry using bagpipes with a delayed star-formation history model (with both free redshift and fixed z = 4.0148); subtract foreground galaxy light in F277W using GALFIT to place apertures and fit SEDs of five faint companions.
key_parameters: Six delayed SFH parameters: log10(M_*/M_sun), SFR, A_V, system age, metallicity (Z/Z_sun), ionization parameter (U)
GALFIT single Sersic profile: R_e ~ 0.21'', n ~ 1.2, b/a ~ 0.7
assumptions: Calzetti et al. (2000) dust attenuation law
Flat LCDM cosmology (H0 = 67.7 km s^-1, Omega_0 = 0.31, T_cmb = 2.725 K)

recipe.goal: Test gravitational lensing hypothesis via ring subtraction, foreground SED fitting, and Einstein mass calculation
recipe.method: Subtract 1.1x F182M from F200W to isolate central emission, derive a flux correction factor of 1.87, fit central photometry in bagpipes as a foreground lens (0.1 < z < 2.0), and compute projected Einstein mass and stellar-to-total mass ratio.
key_parameters: Einstein radius theta_E = 0.25'' (and conservative 0.2''), source redshift z = 4.0148, lens redshift z = 1.66

score_reason: All archival data products (MAST JWST/HST mosaics, CANUCS DR1 spectrum, ALCS ALMA continuum map) are publicly available, and the extracted multi-band aperture photometry is tabulated directly in Table 2, making the bagpipes SED fits and lensing calculations straightforward to reproduce despite minor unstated priors and ALMA flux extraction details.
rediscovery_reason: All underlying datasets and the extracted multi-band photometry (Table 2) are public, the software stack (bagpipes, photutils, stpsf, GALFIT, CARTA) is open-source, and the main claims rely on quantitative numeric results (photometric redshifts, stellar masses, SFRs, dust mass, and Einstein mass ratio).
